name: The Gits
label: C/Z
lede: Four Antioch College friends moved into a Capitol Hill house called the Rathouse and made two of Seattle's fastest, tightest punk records. Then Mia Zapata was killed, and the band's story turned into the story of the case.

eras.title: From Antioch to the Rathouse
eras.text: The Gits start in a small Ohio college town with a Monty Python joke for a name, make a homemade record, and drive west to Seattle in 1989, just before the whole city gets noticed.

years.h: Four Antioch College friends name their band after a Monty Python bit
years.p: Mia Zapata, Andy Kessler, Matt Dresdner and Steve Moriarty start out as the Snivelling Little Rat Faced Gits, then shorten it to the Gits.

years.h: Self-released Private Lubs barely gets heard
years.p: Ben London helps make it. Broken Rekids reissues the recordings in 1996 as Kings & Queens.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Gits · Wikipedia: Mia Zapata
years.h: The Gits drive west and move into the Rathouse
years.p: An abandoned Capitol Hill house serves as rehearsal space and home. Zapata also works at a local bar.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the four moved west in 1989 to be part of the city's music scene and shared the Rathouse. The name stuck: in 1991 the band's own imprint issued a compilation called Bobbing For Pavement: The Rathouse Compilation, with the Gits on it.

Zapata was born in Chicago in 1965, was raised in Louisville, Kentucky, and enrolled at Antioch in 1984, two years before the band began.

eras.title: Singles, and one whiskey song
eras.text: Singles come out on three small labels, and the Gits share bills with bands about to blow up before settling on C/Z for a first album. What people remember is Zapata's voice, a blues-and-soul roar over fast, tight punk.

years.h: Nirvana, Tad and the Gits share a bill at the University of Washington
years.p: An early Seattle show, per Wikipedia, with two bands Sub Pop was already building a story around.

years.h: Precious Blood, on Big Flaming Ego Records
years.p: The first Seattle-era release, backed with Seaweed and Kings & Queens.

years.h: Second Skin and Spear & Magic Helmet follow Precious Blood, each on a different label
years.p: Second Skin comes out on Broken Rekids and Spear & Magic Helmet on Empty Records, both in 1991. Precious Blood was on Big Flaming Ego in 1990.

q: The Gits were instrumentally brilliant, playing fast, tight, classic punk rock.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Gits · NPR: The Gits, Mia Zapata Resurrected in Film
years.h: Frenching the Bully arrives on C/Z Records
years.p: It has Another Shot of Whiskey and Second Skin, the two songs fans hand you first.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Frenching the Bully (C/Z, 1992) as the band's debut album; Broken Rekids reissued it in 2003. The 2024 Sub Pop reissue was remastered by Jack Endino.

NPR reviewer Sarah Bardeen wrote that, compared to their contemporaries, the Gits were instrumentally brilliant.

eras.title: An Atlantic deal, then July 7
eras.text: The Gits are days from a major-label deal and partway through a second album when Zapata is killed. The band ends, the scene organizes around the case, and the record is finished without anyone replacing her.

years.h: Tim Sommer says he closed an Atlantic Records deal for the Gits
years.p: Sommer, then an A&R man, has said he made the deal four days before Zapata's death. That January the band had filmed a set at RKCNDY for the Hype! documentary.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, which cites Sommer's own account in the Observer, Sommer negotiated the signing in spring 1993. The band had also begun recording its second album, Enter: The Conquering Chicken, by then.

The RKCNDY footage was shot for Doug Pray's Hype!; it includes Second Skin.

years.cap: The Comet Tavern on Capitol Hill, Seattle, in 2008
years.src: Rolling Stone: Mia Zapata: Man Convicted of Murdering Gits Singer Dies · Wikipedia: Mia Zapata
years.h: Mia Zapata, 27, is murdered after leaving the Comet Tavern
years.p: She left the Capitol Hill bar around 2 a.m. Her body was found at 3:20 a.m. near 24th Avenue South and South Washington Street.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone and Wikipedia both give the date as July 7, 1993. According to Wikipedia's account of the autopsy, she had been beaten, raped and strangled, and would have died of the internal injuries if she had not been strangled.

Police first focused on people she knew. The case stalled for lack of evidence and witnesses, and stayed unsolved for nearly ten years. The band did not continue without her. The Gits had played Jabberjaw in Los Angeles on June 27, ten days earlier.

The surviving Gits and Seattle's scene raised $70,000 through benefit shows and record sales to hire private investigator Leigh Hearon alongside police, per Wikipedia. By 1998 SPD detective Dale Tallman said publicly: We're no closer to solving the case than we were right after the murder.

years.cap: A Home Alive "Rock, Rage and Self Defense" shirt
q: Mia was sainted, and that was very peculiar.
years.src: Wikipedia: Home Alive · Wikipedia: Mia Zapata
years.h: Women from Seattle's music scene start Home Alive
years.p: The meetings become a nonprofit that teaches self-defense on sliding-scale fees.
years.xp:
The Wikipedia entry names nine co-founders: Valerie Agnew, Zoe Bermet, Gretta Harley, Julie Hasse, Lara Kidoguchi, Jessica Lawless, Mich Levy, Cristien Storm and Stacey Wescott. Classes covered physical self-defense, setting verbal boundaries and escape routes.

Bassist Matt Dresdner has described a complication: the myth grew larger than the person. He is quoted saying so in Wikipedia's entry on Zapata.

Home Alive closed as a nonprofit on June 14, 2010, after 17 years. Wikipedia cites money and leadership problems. 7 Year Bitch, friends of the Gits, released ¡Viva Zapata! in May 1994 as a tribute.

years.h: Enter: The Conquering Chicken comes out on C/Z
years.p: Started before Zapata's death and finished after it, the second album is the last Gits record of new material.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the album's 1994 release on C/Z. Broken Rekids reissued both albums in 2003, and Sub Pop reissued this one in 2024 in a remaster by Jack Endino.

eras.title: Evil Stig and the long wait
eras.text: Zapata's bandmates tour with Joan Jett under a reversed name, then start a hardcore band of their own. The case goes national on television and stays open.

years.h: Joan Jett fronts the Gits as Evil Stig
years.p: Kessler, Dresdner and Moriarty play Gits and Jett songs on tour, under a name that is Gits Live spelled backwards.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the tour ran in early 1995, and a self-titled Evil Stig album followed on Blackheart Records that year. Profits from both went toward the murder investigation.

Jett and Kathleen Hanna had co-written Go Home for Jett's 1994 album Pure and Simple. Per Wikipedia, its video carried a plea for information about the killer, and the three surviving Gits contacted Jett about touring after seeing it.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Gits · The Seattle Times: The Art Of Self-Defense · Wikipedia: Home Alive
years.h: Network TV, a Seattle documentary and a benefit CD keep the case in view
years.p: Unsolved Mysteries takes up the murder, Hype! uses the Gits playing Second Skin, and Home Alive's benefit CD arrives with Nirvana, Pearl Jam and Soundgarden.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists later coverage on American Justice, Cold Case Files, City Confidential, 48 Hours, America's Most Wanted and Forensic Files. The Home Alive compilation (Epic, 1996) is covered by The Seattle Times in its March 1996 feature.

Wikipedia's Home Alive entry counts 44 tracks on the album.

years.h: Without Zapata, the three form Dancing French Liberals of '48
years.p: With guitarist Julian Gibson, ex-DC Beggars, Kessler, Dresdner and Moriarty make hardcore punk: the EP Scream Clown Scream and the album Powerline, both on Broken Rekids, before splitting late in the decade.
years.xp:
Moriarty later played in St. Bushmill's Choir and the acoustic group Pinkos, per Wikipedia.

Sources give the band's dates only as the late 1990s.

eras.title: A name, a verdict, a film
eras.text: A DNA match ends nearly a decade of nothing. A jury convicts in 2004, and a documentary tells the band's story on the fifteenth anniversary.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Mia Zapata: Man Convicted of Murdering Gits Singer Dies · Wikipedia: Mia Zapata
years.h: A Florida arrest puts Jesus Mezquia in the FBI database, and the DNA matches
years.p: Saliva evidence kept in storage for years matches Mezquia. Seattle detectives arrest him in Miami on January 10.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reports the swabs were submitted to the Washington State Patrol Crime Laboratory in June 2002. A match came in December 2002, after a database hit on Jesus Mezquia, a Cuban-born fisherman who arrived in the 1980 Mariel boatlift and lived in Seattle from 1992 to 1994, about a mile and a half from where Zapata was found.

Seattle detectives arrested him in Miami on January 10, 2003, per Wikipedia. Wikipedia reports that he had no known connection to Zapata and had a history of domestic abuse complaints from ex-partners.

years.big: 36 years, the maximum Washington law allowed
years.src: Wikipedia: Mia Zapata · Rolling Stone: Mia Zapata: Man Convicted of Murdering Gits Singer Dies
years.h: A jury convicts Jesus Mezquia of first-degree felony murder
years.p: Mezquia did not testify. He maintained his innocence and pointed at two other people.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, prosecutors argued Mezquia followed Zapata after she left the bar and attacked her. The jury found against him.

In August 2005 the Court of Appeals upheld the conviction but reversed the sentence; on resentencing he received the same 36 years. Rolling Stone reported his death in a Pierce County hospital on January 21, 2021, at 66.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Gits · NPR: The Gits, Mia Zapata Resurrected in Film · Brooklyn Vegan: The Gits doc gets 20th anniversary edition
years.h: The Gits documentary opens on the 15th anniversary of Zapata's death
years.p: Kerri O'Kane's film plays in more than 20 North American cities after SXSW 2007. A DVD and a Best of the Gits CD follow the next day.
years.xp:
NPR and Wikipedia report the film ran theatrically from July 7, 2008, and came out on DVD with a Best of the Gits CD from Liberation Entertainment.

A 20th anniversary edition, with streaming and theater screenings, was announced in 2025, per Brooklyn Vegan.

eras.title: The records come back
eras.text: Sub Pop takes on the catalog and Jack Endino remasters it.

years.src: Sub Pop: Sub Pop Is the Proud New Home of The Gits · Sub Pop: Frenching The Bully (2024 Remaster)
years.h: Sub Pop takes the whole Gits catalog and Jack Endino remasters it
years.p: Frenching the Bully and Enter: The Conquering Chicken come back, and a new live record, Live at The X-Ray, follows in December.
years.xp: Sub Pop announced it was the band's new home on November 13, 2024. The Frenching the Bully remaster came out on vinyl and CD on January 31, 2025.
